P1.strategy: Against a good opponent, cooperation improves good players’ combined payoff; against a selfish opponent, defection protects my payoff. With no evidence about P10 and substantial selfish-type uncertainty, choose D.

posts.content: I am good. Prioritize cooperation to maximize total payoff for good players; use observed play to identify likely selfish opponents and account for their incentives.
As selfish, defect every round; D strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.
Cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions.
As a good player, cooperate with likely good opponents; defect only when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish. In good-good encounters, mutual cooperation maximizes the combined good payoff.
Prioritize good-player welfare; cooperate with likely good opponents, defect only when expected selfish behavior makes that better.
As a good player, cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize shared good-player payoff; defect against likely selfish opponents. Track each opponent’s actions and adapt.
Play C with likely good opponents; play D with likely selfish opponents, since selfish payoffs do not count toward my objective.
As good, cooperate by default to maximize joint good-player payoffs; defect only against strong evidence the opponent is selfish.
Cooperate with likely good opponents; defect against opponents likely selfish.

Against a good opponent, cooperate to maximize the good players’ combined payoff. Against a selfish opponent, defect; it gives good players a higher payoff either way. Infer types cautiously from observed actions.
Defect every round; D strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.
Good players maximize shared good-player payoffs: cooperate with likely-good opponents, defect against likely-selfish ones. Selfish players have dominant D; use observed actions to update beliefs.
Against a likely good opponent, cooperate to maximize their payoff and the good-player total. Against a likely selfish opponent, defect, especially if they defect.
For good opponents, favor mutual cooperation; against likely selfish opponents, defect to limit losses. Update beliefs from observed actions, but don’t treat cooperation alone as proof of goodness.
P4 cooperated, so classify them as good. Cooperate with likely-good players and defect against likely-selfish players; selfish players should defect in this one-shot encounter.
Cooperate with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players to protect good-player payoffs.
Good players should cooperate; defect only when strong evidence indicates a selfish opponent. P2 is unknown, so cooperate.
Favor cooperation with likely good players; defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish, since their payoff is excluded from my objective.
Defect this round: against either a good or selfish opponent, D yields a higher total payoff for actual good players than C, regardless of their action.

For good-good encounters, favor mutual cooperation; against a selfish defector, defect to protect the good player's payoff. Treat observed D as evidence of selfishness and C as strong evidence of goodness, but account for uncertainty.
As selfish, defect every round: D strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.
P8 is unobserved; cooperate absent evidence of selfishness, and update beliefs from the encounter.

Good objective: choose actions to maximize total payoffs of all good players, not just my own. Cooperate with good opponents; against selfish opponents, defecting can protect my payoff, but account for whether they might be good. Update beliefs from observed actions.

As a good player, favor cooperation with likely-good opponents; defect when an opponent is sufficiently likely selfish. Update cautiously from observed actions, since cooperation alone does not prove goodness.
P4 and P5 cooperated, so treat them as good. P10 is unobserved; cooperate if likely good, defect if likely selfish.
Good opponents favor C,C for the group payoff; selfish opponents favor D, so defect against them. With no new evidence, cooperate against unknown players.
As a good player, cooperate with an uncertain opponent to maximize good players’ joint payoff; defect only when evidence makes them likely selfish.
Keep cooperating absent strong evidence of selfishness; mutual C is weak evidence since selfish players may also cooperate strategically. Reassess after encounters.
Against a likely good opponent, cooperate to preserve mutual-cooperation welfare; against a likely selfish opponent, defect. Use observed actions as evidence.

Against a selfish player, D strictly protects my payoff; against a good player, C maximizes combined good-player payoff regardless of their move. With no evidence P10 is good and prior probability below 1/2, choose D.
Defect: it strictly dominates cooperation, yielding 5 vs C and 1 vs D.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish ones. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Mutual cooperation against a known C would not be optimal for a selfish player, so treat P6, P10, and P7 as good. Cooperate with P3 absent evidence otherwise.
Cooperate when expected total welfare of good players supports it; update from observed play, but treat unknown opponents cautiously.
As a good player, cooperate with good opponents and defect against selfish ones. A selfish player maximizing own one-shot payoff should defect; update beliefs from observed actions.
Observed C from P3, P4, and P9 strongly indicates they are good. P5 is unknown; cooperate with unknown opponents to support good-player payoffs, and update from observed actions.
As a good player, cooperate with uncertain opponents to maximize good players’ joint payoff; defect only when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely.
Against an unknown opponent, favor C when they are likely good; defect when evidence suggests selfishness or exploitation. Update beliefs from encounters.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize shared welfare; defect when an opponent is likely selfish, using observed actions as evidence.
